outcome: mother-to-child transmission (MTCT) of hepatitis B virus (HBV)
cohort: The study included 143 HBsAg-positive women who underwent amniocentesis and 605 HBsAg-positive women without amniocentesis, matched based on maternal viral loads, antiviral therapy regimens, and delivery dates.
finding: Amniocentesis significantly increases the risk of mother-to-child transmission of HBV in HBsAg-positive women, with maternal HBV DNA ≥ 7.0 log₁₀ IU/mL and HBeAg positivity identified as additional risk factors.
